rounds.content:
Written test (1 hr): 
1.​ 10 Questions about basic stats,  
2.​ 10 Questions about pandas, python code (given a function what it will 
return or give syntax error, these kind of basic questions) 
3.​ 10 Questions about Finance.(I had no knowledge about these questions, so 
I just took a random guess for every question)

Round 1 (25-30 mins): 
1.​ Basic Regression Questions like multicollinearity, Lasso and Ridge, left and 
Right skewed distribution difference, All the regression model assumptions 
etc. 
2.​ Why do you want to join QRT? 
3.​ What was your role in the previous company and why did you leave? 
4.​ Case:  How will you predict the Corn Price, what will be the features you 
will consider? 
(The last question was almost asked to everyone, but with changed 
commodities, someone was asked about rice, wheat, crude oil, metal etc. All 
these kinds of questions share a similar approach/Framework. You need to 
consider Demand and Supply side features, Macroeconomic features, and 
some other factors. You can ask GPT about it about the Framework)

Round 2 (2-3 mins): 
1.​ It was a rapid-fire round.
2.​ I was working in the defence domain before coming to PGDBA, so 
they just asked me about what the Lnt Defence model is to earn 
money and what features will be helpful to determine the Defence 
industry growth.

Round 3 (30-40mins): (Completely Finance Based) 
1.​ It was an online round in which a guy from Europe joined in. 
2.​ I was given a case/situation:​
Suppose there were only 2 markets (China & US) for trading in the whole 
world and one commodity is being traded in both the markets at the same 
price and in China market supply is lower than demand and in the US 
market supply is higher than demand. 
3.​ So, do you think Trade should happen between these two markets if the 
price of commodities is same in both markets? 
4.​ At what price differential, do you think the trade between the market will 
start? 
5.​ So, what do you think will happen in future, will this trend continue, the 
price of commodities change or not? 
6.​ What will be your investing strategy and at what level of risk you will pull 
out of the trade?

rounds.content:
Directly asked me a question. 
Suppose there are two countries in this world – US & China – US has a surplus of 
commodities inventory & Chn with a deficit. How would you create a trading 
strategy if you have this situation? 
This was a tricky question where I had to frame a question to myself. I explained 
by saying about the supply demand curve in both places – Prices going up in 
China while down in the US. First explained imp arb – buying physical inventory 
in the US & selling in China. However, he said a financial trader won’t do so. 
(Obviously!!) 
He asked me to think deeper in terms of Futures. I said something related to that. 
He asked how the situation is if there are two exchanges v/s single exchange. 
Hinted me to arbitrages. Asked how I would think about the dynamics of 
production in both the countries. 
In between he asked me if I did my bachelors in Economics to which I denied. He 
asked if I studied Eco. in my post grad, to which I explained to him that my

Winning case comps gives you confidence and that helps. Sunpharma asks to give 
an excel sheet of students with casecomps they have won and POR for shortlist. 
How well you know them is for sure important, but topics should be like you have 
solved some business problem, not just build a model on kaggle dataset. And 
there should be variety in topics.

numbers. They will discuss the numbers in detail. 
3.​ Mostly it’s about the fit and vibe, if they like you, they take you. They will 
keep the interview very interactive, you will not feel any pressure.  
 
Case comps: Not that much. But good to have 2-3 case comps in your CV. 
Winning case comps gives you confidence and that helps. Sunpharma asks to give 
an excel sheet of students with casecomps they have won and POR for shortlist. 
How well you know them is for sure important, but topics should be like you have 
solved some business problem, not just build a model on kaggle dataset. And 
there should be variety in topics.

rounds.content:
Prashant Bisht 
 
PF selected us based on our CV. What I felt based on the people selected for the 
interview, they have 2 projects in common. 1 classification(Finance fraud/loan 
default) and other RAG projects. I had both of them in my CV. There were 2 
panels. Each panel had 2 persons. One asked related to LLM’s and RAG. And 
others asked about traditional ML related to classification. 
 
Since there are 2 teams in PF one is the credit risk modelling team, so 
classification. And others are the GenAI team, LLM and RAG. 
 
1st interviewer:   
1. Explain how the pre-training is done in BERT?  He was expecting “masked 
language modelling” and “next sentence prediction”. Then counter question: 
2. How BERT does classification? He was expecting BERT architecture. CLS 
token, probability distribution over entire vocabulary using softmax. He asked 
BERT since I had mentioned BERT multiple times in my CV.  
3. What is SVD? How is it used in the recommendation model? Since I had a 
project on movie recommendation using SVD. Prepare the meaning of each 
matrix also. A = U sigma V(transpose). What is U, V and sigma?

4. Explain your RAG project.

This was a complete technical interview, all questions asked were CV based. 
 
The 2nd interviewer asked about the ML questions.  
1. The model is performing well on the training set but not on the test set. Why?
2. ⁠Suppose a model is trained on 3 years data, let’s say 2017-2020. It performed 
well on the 2021 data. But fails to perform well on the 2022 data. Why? (Prepare 
this well with an example)  
3. How will you explain this model not performing well on 2022 data to a 
business person?  
4. ⁠There is a classification model that is giving good ROC-AUC value. But the 
model performance is not good. Why? ROC-AUC might not be the best metric for 
the model. if there is class imbalance then ROC-AUC is unreliable, PR-AUC 
should be checked. 
5. He countered that, if roc-auc is good, shouldn’t pr-auc also be good? 
 
I didn’t feel at any point the interviews went wrong technically.

rounds.content:
Sushrut Joshi 
 
Interview one: (2 guys from data science team) 
Q: How many years of work experience do you have? What did you do at your job? And 
some other questions related to workex. 
A: workex 3 yr, analytics background etc etc… 
Q: Analytics case study:- given many factors around farming of berries, also gave 
multiple hierarchies for time series forecasting (example: region, farmer, time 
etc). decide 1) at what level to forecast, 2) how to forecast. Then got in depth of 
this as why you chose this approach, what would happen if you change some 
things etc. 
A: I fumbled a bit, but they will help if you try telling your approach. They just 
checked whether we could approach the problem in a structured manner or not 
(which I think I was able to :) ) 
Q: basic DL/ NLP questions in a rapid fire manner: transformers, finetuning, 
attention-self attention models, etc. 
A: One should be thorough with all these concepts. 
Q: Do you use LLMs in your projects? Which models did you use?  
A: I thought this was a trick question, but I answered it honestly. Basically at 
work they call all your LLMs to do majority work and what I sensed was he 
wanted to know which models I use and for which tasks. With that I mentioned 
Agentic mode of chat GPT (just to give him a hook). 
Q: Do you know about agentic AI? 
A: Yes, I told  what I read the night before… 
Q: Do you know about RAG? 
A: told whatever I read the night before… 
Q: follow up questions on RAG: why do we use it? Why can't we feed everything 
to LLM and get answers? How do we retrieve the data?
A: One can answer these questions by giving a 3-4 hr read about RAG.​
(I didn’t have any project on RAG, but as it was mentioned in JDF, I read about 
the stuff). 
Q: coding question: simple data manipulation, they gave me a small dataset in 
json, asked me to load  it, filter it, merge, groupby etc.

rounds.content:
A: normal prepared answer. 
Q: lets test your traditional ML knowledge, what is regression? When not to use 
this? Difference between SLR and polynomial regression? When do we use 
polynomial regression? What is logistic regression? How can we do the multi 
class classification using logistic regression? 
A: answered all the questions and the interviewer seemed satisfied.  
Q: Do you know about SVM? What are support vectors? What are different 
margins? How does changing the hyper parameter in the SVM equation change 
the classification? 
A: answered all the questions and the interviewer seemed satisfied.  
Q: Questions with respect to classification, how do we choose the number of 
clusters in k means? Explain elbow method in short? What is there on y- axis 
during the elbow method? Which clustering do we use in which case? (K-means, 
hierarchical, DBSCAN). Limitations of each methods? 
A: answered all the questions and the interviewer seemed satisfied. 
Q: Are you comfortable with Bayesian ML techniques?  
A: I know where to use it and how to use it, but I'm not comfortable with the 
equation and stuff. (He then didn’t ask on this topic)
Q: Are you comfortable with boosting algorithms? (yes…). How does the XGBoost 
algorithm work? Difference between XGBoost and CatBoost? 
A:  answered all the questions and the interviewer seemed satisfied. 
Q: Another guy asked a coding question (based on hashing):- given a string, you 
have to give output of the letter which gets repeated first. Example: “swish”à s is 
repeated first, hence output is “s”. “saasw”à her a is repeated first hence output is 
“a”. “halo”à none is repeated,hence output is “None”. 
A: coded on jupyter notebook (screen shared). Used hashing for this. ​
follow up questions on code, is it optimised? What is the time complexity of this 
code? 
(they try to look at your approach, if you are not confident with syntax, you can 
ask them if you can use the internet for syntax, they may allow, discuss the 
approach first). 
​
Third Interview: (India head- cultural fit) 
Normal interaction with India head, discussed things about location, company 
objectives, policy, joining date etc. ​
He indirectly mentioned that they need people for full time and are hiring for full 
time and not intern(basically giving PPO hints on the spot)  
Note: I had given nearly every company’s interview (almost all rounds), Auxo’s 
interview was one of the most comprehensive interviews covering almost all the 
topics. This might be due to the fact that they mostly give ppo on the spot.

rounds.content:
Round 1 - 
1st introduction. Then he took my credit card default project. Asked objective and how 
exactly I did that. Why F beta score, etc. Then he gave me a scenario that I am working in a 
bank and have access to all this data. How will I approach the same project? How will I 
collect data and how will I merge them, how will I define the business metric etc. 
Then he gave me a scenario, wherein I have to find fraud in the ecommerce business. But 
this is a fresh project - so you have to define fraud, tell the approach to collect the data, and 
how to validate it. Caveat is that it has not been done before. Lots of cross questioning 
happened in this case 
Then he asked me some technical questions from my CV (the keywords) and in general. 
Like when to choose a neural net and when to go for Logistic regression, etc..

Round 2 - 
It was sort of a leadership round and compatibility check round. It happened with senior 
leadership. They explained my vision of Games24, and asked me what I understood about 
Games and why I wanted to join it. Why I am fascinated about the product. Then they asked 
me if I would prefer updating myself on cutting edge AI ML stuff or just learn that which is 
being required by the current project. They were asking questions to understand if I will take 
initiatives, etc. Then he asked, let's say you deployed a model, but its not working and you 
are not getting results, i.e. business metrics are not showing success. What will be your 
approach and how will you handle that? 
Then he asked if I had any questions - and then we interacted for some time.

rounds.content:
Round 1: Case Presentation (~30 min) 
Case: NYC Hourly Cab Demand Index Forecasting 
●​ Approach: Used SARIMAX (aggregation) + Random Forest Regression 
(disaggregation) to forecast demand indices with dual seasonality (daily and weekly). 
Exogenous variables included subway ridership, precipitation, and temperature. 
1.​ What kind of variable is 'hour of the day' (nominal categorical)? What about the 
demand index (discrete/count data)? 
2.​ How would you statistically measure the association between a nominal variable and 
a count variable? 
3.​ Why did you aggregate data daily instead of weekly? 
4.​ How would you incorporate subway ridership into a forecast when future data isn’t 
available? 
5.​ Would lag 2 for subway ridership show a similar pattern? Why or why not?

Data science case study – Usecase was from NLP 
There are several news coming from trading, geo-political scenario. You have to go through 
all the articles for trading purpose. In those articles too, some were small and some were 
quite long. We have to devise some technique that could trade 1 stock based on that news.

rounds.content:
Puzzle: Camel and Banana Puzzle 
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/puzzle-15-camel-and-banana-puzzle/ 
 
A person has 3000 bananas and a camel. The person wants to transport the maximum 
number of bananas to a destination which is 1000 KMs away, using only the camel as a 
mode of transportation. The camel cannot carry more than 1000 bananas at a time and eats 
a banana every km it travels. What is the maximum number of bananas that can be 
transferred to the destination using only camel (no other mode of transportation is allowed). 
 
Approached by incrementally increasing drop point 
Later found that it's already solved in GFG 
 
Puzzle: Tapered circular Rod of some length need to find the midpoint, we can burn the rod 
from any end 
Burn from both the ends simultaneously 
Assumption: Rod consumption is directly proportional to volume
